questions.stem: Ethan writes range(1,4) and expects 1,2,3,4; why is 4 missing?

questions.subject: PYTHON
questions.learningObjective: Explain why while n: stops at zero.
questions.stem: Fiona explains why `while n:` stops when n reaches 0.

answer.exemplar: Zero is falsy, so the condition becomes false when n reaches 0. The loop terminates without needing an explicit comparison.

questions.explanation: Zero is falsy, making the condition false. The loop ends naturally when n reaches 0.
